name: Aston Martin DB2
description:
The first car of David Brown's Aston Martin: a Claude Hill chassis carrying the twin-cam straight-six W.O. Bentley had designed for Lagonda, which Brown had bought in the same year and largely for the engine. It ran at Le Mans in 1949 before it had a name, and was in production by 1950.

Four hundred and eleven were built to 1953. The competition cars took the three-litre class at Le Mans in 1950 and 1951, third overall in 1951, and a class win on the 1951 Mille Miglia. The DB2/4 that followed added two occasional seats and a hatchback tailgate — one of the first anywhere — and it was those that ran the 1955 Mille Miglia in British privateers' hands.
